title: Moderation and interaction effects
summary: Moderation means the strength of an effect depends on a third variable; it is modelled with an interaction term and is a different idea from mediation.

body.text: [[moderation]] means that the effect of X on Y depends on the level of a moderator W: for example, usefulness may matter more for intention among experienced users. It is modelled with an interaction term.

body.explanation: b₃ is the interaction: the change in the effect of X on Y for each unit increase in W. With the interaction in the model, b₁ is the effect of X when W = 0 (the mean, if W is standardised), not an average effect.

body.text: In PLS-SEM the interaction term between latent constructs is built with the product-indicator, the two-stage or the orthogonalising approach; Henseler and Chin (2010) compared them, and the two-stage approach is a common default (Hair et al. 2022). In CB-SEM latent interactions need specialised estimators. A categorical moderator such as group membership leads to multigroup analysis (next lesson).
SEM Studio does not estimate interaction effects yet; the feature is planned. Use R packages such as cSEM or seminr for moderation analysis, and report which approach you used.
body.title: Not available in SEM Studio

mistake.title: Confusing moderation with mediation
mistake.text: A mediator transmits an effect (X → M → Y); a moderator changes the strength of an effect (W changes X → Y). They answer different questions and are tested differently (Baron & Kenny 1986).

checks.question: In Y = .40·X + .10·W + .15·(X·W), with standardised X and W, what does .15 mean?

options.text: The effect of X on Y increases by .15 for every standard deviation increase in W.
options.feedback: Correct. At W = +1 SD the effect of X is about .55, at W = −1 SD about .25.

options.text: W mediates 15% of the effect of X.
options.feedback: Interactions do not split an effect into routes; that is mediation.

options.text: The average effect of X is .15.
options.feedback: With standardised W, .40 is the effect of X at the average of W.

checks.explanation: Interaction = effect of one variable depends on another.

options.text: The effect of usefulness on intention is stronger for experienced users.
options.feedback: Correct. Experience changes the strength of an effect.

options.text: Ease of use increases usefulness, which in turn increases intention.

options.feedback: That is a direct effect of experience.
